licenses.issuingAuthority: Competent Authority (EO/CMC) under the Local Government Department, with final approval by the MCEO; technical scrutiny by HQ/STP, MTP, ATP, DM/HDM, JE/BI

portal.name: Invest Punjab Single Window Portal (eNaksha Scrutiny Engine - Auto Byelaws Compliance / Auto-DCR)

timeline.basis: 45-day statutory timeline (Right to Business Act, under which deemed approval also applies)
timeline.text: Most applications are approved within the 45-day statutory timeline. A mandatory site inspection by the building inspector is completed within 5 days of application; delays occur only when submitted documents are incomplete, leading to rejection or return for resubmission.

documents: Copy of CLU (Change of Land Use) approval
Copy of Revenue Plan basis for CLU
Copy of previous approved map / Regularization report
NOC from owners of adjacent properties for basement construction

deemedApproval.text: Deemed approval exists under the Right to Business Act with a 45-day timeline, but the expert confirmed it is rarely invoked since most applications are processed and approved within the statutory timeline itself; the provision exists as a safeguard.

validity.text: The Building Plan Approval is a one-time approval for the construction lifecycle and does not require renewal; a separate Occupancy Certificate is issued after construction is completed.

fees.text: Fees are fixed based on covered area and land parcel, not on industry risk category (Red/Orange/Green); exact fee figures were not given. Registration for engineers and building supervisors is free of cost.

steps.title: Submit Building Plan Application on Invest Punjab Portal
steps.note: Submitted via the eNaksha Scrutiny Engine with auto byelaws compliance checking.

steps.title: Submit application with processing fee / balance fees
Application routed to Dealing Hand for scrutiny
steps.note: Projects above ₹25 Cr go to HQ; below ₹25 Cr stay at district level.

steps.title: Completeness check by Dealing Hand
steps.note: If incomplete, returned to applicant within 1 day.

steps.title: Application moves to Competent Authority (EO/CMC) for processing
steps.note: Time lapse: 3 days.

steps.title: First observations check by Competent Authority
steps.note: If observations exist, file is sent back to applicant to resolve.

steps.title: Field & Technical Report stage across multiple departments
steps.note: Reviewed by HQ/STP, MTP, ATP, DM/HDM, JE/BI; time lapse 7 days; comments shown to EO/CMC.

steps.title: Second observations check after technical reports
steps.note: If observations exist, file is sent back to applicant.

steps.title: Application processed at Competent Authority (EO/CMC) level
Fee Calculation stage across departments
steps.note: Routed with a "Back to source option" to JE/BI, DM/HDM, ATP/AME, and MTP/ME for fee calculation.

steps.title: Application returns to Competent Authority for Technical Report generation
Application moves to MCEO for Approval/Rejection
Final observations check
steps.note: If observations exist, application is rejected and sent back; if none, fees are raised by the Competent Authority.

steps.title: Payment link sent to applicant
Final Approval granted after fee submission

remarks: Most applicants are satisfied with the process, as approvals are received within the 45-day timeline.
Most applicants use registered consultants/architects to submit applications, but the process is user-friendly enough for self-submission.
A functional help desk is available to assist applicants with any issues.

findings.text: If land falls under the jurisdiction of Railways, Defence, Airport Authority, or Forest Department, the applicant must obtain the NOC offline from that department and upload it manually, since these departments are not integrated with the Single Window System.

Obtaining offline NOCs from national-level departments (Railways, Defence, Airport Authority) adds to compliance burden and delays, and is described as a burdensome activity driven by national-level Acts/Rules.
CLU and Building Plan Approval were previously clubbed, which reduced duplication, but were later segregated at the state level, increasing the number of approvals required.

The expert recommends expediting integration of Railways, Defence, Airport Authority, and other national-level departments with the Single Window System to eliminate offline NOC requirements and reduce applicant visits.
The expert recommends re-clubbing CLU and Building Plan Approval, at least for layouts, to reduce duplication and time.
The expert recommends reviewing the documentation checklist to identify and eliminate redundant, non-critical documents.
The department uses Auto-DCR (Digital Plan Scrutiny) for automated validation of building plans against regulations.
The Invest Punjab Portal is integrated with multiple state-level departments through API sharing, creating a single application point.
A separate online grievance portal (PGRS) is available for applicants to raise complaints, which are resolved on a priority basis.
The previous clubbing of CLU and Building Plan Approval is cited as a best practice that reduced duplication and is still applicable for layouts.
A mandatory site inspection is conducted by the building inspector within 5 days of application to verify the site and surroundings, required in all cases regardless of land category.
Deemed approval exists under the Right to Business Act with a 45-day timeline, but it is rarely invoked as most applications are approved within the statutory timeline.
Delays occur only when submitted documents are incomplete; in such cases the application is rejected or returned for resubmission.
Most applicants are satisfied with the process, as approvals are received within the 45-day timeline.
A functional help desk is available to assist applicants with any issues.
Fees are fixed based on covered area and land parcel, not based on industry risk category (Red/Orange/Green).
Registration is free of cost for engineers and building supervisors.

No ongoing regulatory requirements (e.g., maintaining registers, periodic equipment testing) are mandated after Building Plan Approval; post-approval compliance is handled through separate approvals (e.g., CTO, Fire NOC) by other departments.

gaps.text: Exact fee figures/schedule for Building Plan Approval are not given — only the basis (covered area and land parcel) is described.
No portal URL is given for the Invest Punjab Single Window Portal / eNaksha system.
Individual step time-lapses are given for only a few steps (1 day, 3 days, 7 days) out of the 15-step process; how these reconcile to the overall 45-day statutory timeline is not fully broken down.
No detail is given on penalties or consequences for non-compliance with the approved plan during construction.
Auto-DCR enables automated validation of building plans against byelaws, reducing manual scrutiny subjectivity.
A dedicated online grievance portal (PGRS) handles applicant complaints on a priority basis.
Proposed integration of national-level departments (Railways, Defence, Airport Authority, Forest Department) with the Single Window System to eliminate offline NOC requirements — not yet implemented.
Proposed re-clubbing of CLU and Building Plan Approval (at least for layouts), currently segregated — not yet implemented.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Licensing Authority, Department of Legal Metrology, acting on the report/recommendation of the jurisdictional Inspector, Legal Metrology (ILM) and, for new licenses, a technical ability test committee

portal.name: e-Mapan portal, integrated with the Invest Punjab Single Window System

timeline.basis: Statutory timelines notified under the Punjab Transparency & Accountability in Delivery of Public Services Act, 2018
timeline.text: 30 days for Licenses (Manufacturer, Repairer, Dealer) and Verification services; 21 days for Registration (Manufacturer/Packer/Importer); 45 days for Renewal from receipt of a complete application.

documents: Proof of legal title of premises (sale deed/lease deed/allotment letter/property tax receipt)
Constitution of firm (partnership deed, incorporation certificate, etc.)
Model Approval Certificate from Central Government (for Manufacturer License)
List of Tools & Equipment (for Manufacturer License)
List of Testing Equipment (for Manufacturer License)
Literature of items to be manufactured (for Manufacturer License)
Proof of Financial Status (for Manufacturer License)
Proof of Power Load sanctioned (for Manufacturer License)
Tools and equipment list (for Repairer License)
Loan articles with verification certificate (for Repairer License)
Stock and sales statement (Form LD-4) verified by area Inspector (for Dealer License)
licenses.documentsNote: Requirements vary by sub-service (Manufacturer/Repairer/Dealer license, Registration, and Verification/Re-verification); the documents above are grouped by the sub-service the ED named them under, with common documents applying across all.

deemedApproval.text: The expert confirmed deemed approval is not possible for Legal Metrology services because physical inspection of premises, tools, equipment, and weights is a mandatory statutory requirement that must be completed to ensure compliance.

validity.text: License is valid for a minimum of 1 year and can be renewed for 1 to 5 calendar years, with a current maximum validity of 3 years. A proposal for a "lifetime" license to eliminate repeated renewals is under consideration. Renewal applications must be submitted at least 30 days before expiry, or up to 3 months after expiry with an additional fee of half the prescribed rate.

fees.text: License fees (annual): Manufacturer ₹10,000, Dealer ₹2,000, Repairer ₹4,000. Registration fees: new registration ₹500, amendment ₹100, duplicate license ₹100. Verification fees vary by instrument type, accuracy level, and capacity, but exact figures were not given. No separate inspection charges apply.

steps.title: Applicant submits online application with documents (License)
steps.note: Submitted via Invest Punjab Portal / e-Mapan.

steps.title: Application directed to jurisdictional Inspector, Legal Metrology (ILM)
steps.note: Auto-fetched from Invest Punjab with an auto-generated ID.

steps.title: Inspector scrutinizes application and conducts field visit/spot inspection
steps.note: Communicates deficiencies, verifies original documents, prepares inspection report.

steps.title: Inspector forwards application with recommendations to Licensing Authority
Technical ability test by a committee of at least three members
steps.note: Mandatory in-person assessment of the applicant's competence.

steps.title: Licensing Authority decides to grant or reject the license
steps.note: Based on inspector's report and committee's technical ability test report.

steps.title: Applicant deposits license fee
steps.note: If satisfactory.

steps.title: License issued
steps.note: Issued within 7 days of fee deposit.

steps.title: Licensee submits renewal application (Renewal)
steps.note: At least 30 days before expiry, with prescribed fee and mandatory registers.

steps.title: Inspector verifies records
steps.note: Within 15 days; renewal verification is now paper/document-based only, without physical inspection.

steps.title: Inspector submits report to Licensing Authority
Licensing Authority decides on renewal
steps.note: License renewed or rejected by reasoned order.

steps.title: Applicant presents weight/measure for verification
steps.note: At the office of the Legal Metrology Officer or a designated place (Verification/Re-verification).

steps.title: Officer visits site if instrument cannot be moved
steps.note: User reports at least 30 days in advance.

steps.title: Officer tests and stamps the instrument, issues verification certificate
steps.note: Certificate issued under Schedule XVI.

ed.designation: Assistant Controller, Legal Metrology, Department of Legal Metrology

remarks: The expert confirmed there are no significant problems in the Legal Metrology process; the service has been simplified to a high degree.
Applicants can apply directly without the need for consultants or agents.
Grievances are handled through the central grievance portal; most are resolved within one month.
Penalties range from ₹2,000 to ₹50,000 for non-compliance, such as failure to get instruments verified.

findings.text: Document requirements have been significantly reduced and repetitive documents have been eliminated.
Affidavits have been replaced with self-declarations, reducing third-party dependency.
Physical inspection for renewal has been eliminated; renewal is now processed based only on paper/document verification.
Licenses are now auto-renewed without human intervention, eliminating the need for repeated renewal applications.
The department reduced the number of approval levels from 3 to 2-3, streamlining and expediting the process.
A proposal for a "lifetime" license is under consideration to eliminate repeated renewals entirely; the expert recommends expanding this to all Legal Metrology services.
The expert recommends enabling 100% online application and verification of weights and measures, without the need for physical instrument visits.
Deemed approval is not possible for Legal Metrology services because physical verification of premises, tools, equipment, and weights is a mandatory statutory requirement.
A mandatory technical ability test is conducted by a committee of at least three members to assess a new license applicant's competence in person.
For first-time instrument verification, the applicant must physically bring the instrument to the Inspector's office/camp, or the Inspector visits the site.
Applications from the Invest Punjab portal are auto-fetched into the Legal Metrology department's system with an auto-generated ID.
Applicants can apply directly without the need for consultants or agents.
Grievances are handled through the central grievance portal; most are resolved within one month.
Queries are raised through the portal, and applicants can respond online.
Penalties for non-compliance (e.g., failure to get instruments verified) range from ₹2,000 to ₹50,000.

The expert confirmed there are no significant burdensome activities or pain points in the Legal Metrology process; the service has been simplified to a high degree, with users even questioning why the department made it "so easy."
Renewal applications must be submitted at least 30 days before expiry, but can be submitted up to 3 months after expiry with an additional fee of half the prescribed rate.

gaps.text: Exact verification fees for weights/measures by instrument type, accuracy level, and capacity are not specified — only described as variable.
No portal URL is given for the e-Mapan portal or the Invest Punjab Single Window System.

The ED states "No Physical Visit by Applicant for Application" is required, yet also describes a mandatory in-person Technical Ability Test by a committee and, for first-time instrument verification, the applicant physically bringing the instrument to the Inspector's office — these are not reconciled in the document.
No detail is given on the composition (departmental roles) of the "committee of at least three members" that conducts the technical ability test.
No specific sub-timeline is given for how long the technical ability test itself takes within the overall 30-day License timeline.
Auto-renewal of licenses without human intervention, combined with elimination of physical inspection for renewals (paper-based verification only).
Proposal for a "lifetime" license to eliminate repeated renewals entirely is under consideration but not yet implemented.
